q: Using the Group V (Monumental) rate, compute the Architect's RPF under DAEDS for this project.
n: RPF (DAEDS) = 12% x PCC = 0.12 x P45,000,000 = P5,400,000. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5 (DAEDS = 12% of PCC))
scenario: A private foundation is developing a new city museum. The Project Construction Cost (PCC) is P45,000,000.

q: Under SPP Doc. 202, Group V (Monumental) buildings are officially described as those requiring:
o: Simple, repetitive design with minimal detailing
Extensive structural engineering only, with no aesthetic requirement
Purely decorative treatment with no functional requirement
Consummate design skill and much precise detailing
n: Group V covers "monumental buildings and other facilities requiring consummate design skill and much precise detailing." (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5)

q: Using the same exposition building project, compute the Architect's RPF under DADS.
n: RPF (DADS) = 7.5% x PCC = 0.075 x P60,000,000 = P4,500,000. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5 (DADS = 7.5% of PCC))
scenario: A national government agency is holding an international trade exposition and commissions a new exposition/fair building for the event. The Project Construction Cost (PCC) is P60,000,000.

q: The Group V (Monumental) building-type list closes with a catch-all category described as:
o: "Any building exceeding P50 million in PCC"
"Other structures as determined by the LGU"
n: After naming Exposition & Fair Buildings, Specialized Decorative Buildings, Mausoleums/Memorials/Monuments, and Museums, Group V adds a catch-all: "Buildings of similar nature or use." (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5)

q: Under Group V (Monumental), the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for Detailed Architectural Design Services (DADS) is:
n: Group V's DADS rate is a flat 7.5% of the Project Construction Cost (PCC). (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5)

q: Using the same decorative gateway project, compute the Architect's RPF under DADS.
n: RPF (DADS) = 7.5% x PCC = 0.075 x P3,200,000 = P240,000. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5 (DADS = 7.5% of PCC))
scenario: A private client commissions a specialized decorative ceremonial gateway/arch for a public park. The Project Construction Cost (PCC) is P3,200,000.

q: Using the same memorial monument project, compute the Architect's RPF under DADS.
n: RPF (DADS) = 7.5% x PCC = 0.075 x P8,500,000 = P637,500. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5 (DADS = 7.5% of PCC))
scenario: A local government unit plans to build a war memorial monument honoring fallen soldiers. The Project Construction Cost (PCC) is P8,500,000.

q: A client questions why the Architect's fee percentage for a proposed monument is higher than the rate quoted for a similarly priced single-detached residence. The best explanation, per SPP Doc. 202, is that:
o: Monument projects always cost less to build overall
Government-funded projects are automatically charged higher fees
The Architect is required to shoulder the client's engineering costs
Group V projects demand a greater degree of design skill and precise detailing than Group IV residences, justifying a higher RPF rate
n: The building grouping exists precisely to set fee rates according to the degree of complexity and creative skill required; Group V (12%/7.5%) commands a higher rate than Group IV Residences (10%/6%) because monumental buildings require consummate design skill and precise detailing. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3 and Sec. 6.3.5)

q: Using the Group V (Monumental) rate, compute the Architect's RPF under DAEDS for this exposition building.
n: RPF (DAEDS) = 12% x PCC = 0.12 x P60,000,000 = P7,200,000. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5 (DAEDS = 12% of PCC))
scenario: A national government agency is holding an international trade exposition and commissions a new exposition/fair building for the event. The Project Construction Cost (PCC) is P60,000,000.

q: What does Sec. 6 of the Architect's Guidelines (SPP Doc. 202) primarily govern?
o: Regular Design Services and how the Architect's professional fee is determined
n: Sec. 6, titled "Regular Design Services (SPP Doc. 202)," covers the manner of providing services, methods of compensation, and the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) by building group. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6)

q: Whether the Architect renders services under DAEDS or DADS, the professional responsibility and civil liability of each state-regulated professional involved:
o: Is assumed entirely by the Architect as lead professional
Is waived once the Service Agreement is signed
n: In both DAEDS and DADS arrangements, the professional responsibilities and civil liabilities of each State-regulated professional remain separate; the Architect does not assume the responsibilities/liabilities of the other Registered and Licensed Professionals (RLPs). (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.1)

q: Using the Group V (Monumental) rate, compute the Architect's RPF under DAEDS for this single mausoleum project.
n: RPF (DAEDS) = 12% x PCC = 0.12 x P20,000,000 = P2,400,000, matching the base Group V computation used in the reference sample computation for a mausoleum project. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5 (DAEDS = 12% of PCC))
scenario: An architect is engaged to design a mausoleum complex for a private cemetery developer. The Project Construction Cost (PCC) is P20,000,000.

q: Using the Group V (Monumental) rate, compute the Architect's RPF under DAEDS for this decorative gateway.
n: RPF (DAEDS) = 12% x PCC = 0.12 x P3,200,000 = P384,000. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5 (DAEDS = 12% of PCC))
scenario: A private client commissions a specialized decorative ceremonial gateway/arch for a public park. The Project Construction Cost (PCC) is P3,200,000.

q: Which of the following is NOT among the building types explicitly enumerated under Group V (Monumental)?
o: Housing projects built on a single site using one set of plans
n: Housing projects using a single set of plans on one site fall under Group VII (Housing Projects), not Group V. Group V lists Exposition & Fair Buildings, Specialized Decorative Buildings, Mausoleums/Memorials/Monuments, Museums, and buildings of similar nature or use. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5)

q: Compared to other building groups under SPP Doc. 202 whose RPF is computed via a bracketed, sliding scale of percentages that decrease as PCC increases, Group V's RPF is:
o: Computed only on a per diem basis
Subject to a fixed peso ceiling regardless of PCC
A flat, single percentage of PCC regardless of project cost size
Also bracketed by PCC tier, decreasing at higher cost levels
n: Unlike groups that use a bracketed schedule of decreasing percentages as PCC rises, Group V's RPF is a flat 12% of PCC (DAEDS) and 7.5% of PCC (DADS), applied uniformly no matter the project's cost size. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5)

q: Under SPP Doc. 202, Detailed Architectural Design Services (DADS) is characterized by:
o: A fee limited to expert-witness testimony
A single contract combining all professionals under the Architect
The Owner contracting the Architect and the engineering/allied professionals under separate contracts
A fee based only on a multiple of direct personnel expense
n: DADS involves the Architect and the engineering and allied professionals each executing separate contracts directly with the Owner. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.1.2)

q: The grouping of buildings under Sec. 6.3 of SPP Doc. 202 is intended to:
o: Determine fair remuneration for the Architect based on the degree of complexity and creative skill required
Establish minimum floor area requirements per building type
Determine local government construction permit fees
n: Professional architectural work is classified according to the degree of complexity and creative skill required to meet the Client's requirements within technical, functional, economic, and aesthetic constraints; the building grouping exists to determine the Architect's fair remuneration. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3)

q: An architect is commissioned to design a mausoleum and memorial complex. Under SPP Doc. 202's building grouping, this project's Recommended Professional Fee should be computed using:
n: Mausoleums, memorials, and monuments are expressly enumerated as Group V (Monumental) building types. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5)

q: SPP Doc. 202 (Regular Design Services), which sets out the Group V monumental-building fee schedule, was officially published in the:
o: The National Building Code IRR exclusively
n: The Architect's Guidelines text of SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6, appears in the Official Gazette (Vol. 112, No. 38, September 19, 2016). (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6 (Official Gazette, Vol. 112, No. 38))

q: Using the same mausoleum project, compute the Architect's RPF under DADS.
n: RPF (DADS) = 7.5% x PCC = 0.075 x P20,000,000 = P1,500,000. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5 (DADS = 7.5% of PCC))
scenario: An architect is engaged to design a mausoleum complex for a private cemetery developer. The Project Construction Cost (PCC) is P20,000,000.

q: Under SPP Doc. 202, Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS) is characterized by:
o: Separate contracts between the Owner and each engineering/allied professional
A lump-sum fixed fee regardless of project cost
A single contract between the Architect and Owner, with sub-consultancy contracts between the Architect and the other professionals
A fee computed solely on a per diem basis
n: DAEDS involves a single contract between the Architect and the Owner, with the Architect entering into sub-consultancy contracts with the other professionals working with him/her. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.1.1)

q: Using the Group V (Monumental) rate, compute the Architect's RPF under DAEDS for this memorial monument.
n: RPF (DAEDS) = 12% x PCC = 0.12 x P8,500,000 = P1,020,000. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5 (DAEDS = 12% of PCC))
scenario: A local government unit plans to build a war memorial monument honoring fallen soldiers. The Project Construction Cost (PCC) is P8,500,000.

q: Under Sec. 6.2, the Architect's compensation for Regular Design Services may be based on one or more listed methods. Which of the following is NOT among them?
o: Per Diem, Honorarium Plus Reimbursable Expenses
n: Sec. 6.2 lists Percentage of PCC, Unit Cost Method, Professional Fee plus Expenses, Lump Sum/Fixed Fee, Per Diem/Honorarium Plus Reimbursable Expenses, Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses, and Mixed Methods. "Value Engineering Savings Share" is not one of the listed methods. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.2)

q: The Owner of a proposed monument project wants to deal with a single prime contract covering both architectural and engineering design, leaving the Architect to enter into sub-consultancy contracts with the other professionals. Which manner of providing services applies?
o: Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS)
Lump Sum or Fixed Fee arrangement
Per Diem, Honorarium Plus Reimbursable Expenses arrangement
n: This describes DAEDS: a single contract between the Architect and Owner, with the Architect separately sub-contracting the other engineering and allied professionals. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.1.1)

q: Using the same museum project, compute the Architect's RPF under DADS.
n: RPF (DADS) = 7.5% x PCC = 0.075 x P45,000,000 = P3,375,000. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5 (DADS = 7.5% of PCC))
scenario: A private foundation is developing a new city museum. The Project Construction Cost (PCC) is P45,000,000.

q: Under Group V (Monumental), the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS) is:
n: Group V's DAEDS rate is a flat 12% of the Project Construction Cost (PCC), higher than Group IV's 10% because of the greater design skill and detailing Group V demands. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5)

q: Which of the following is explicitly listed as a Group V (Monumental) building type under SPP Doc. 202?
n: Group V enumerates Exposition & Fair Buildings, Specialized Decorative Buildings, Mausoleums, Memorials & Monuments, Museums, and Buildings of similar nature or use. Row-houses, small apartment houses, and townhouses belong to Group IV (Residences). (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.5)
